'''Eric Jean-Paul Urban''' is a professor of mathematics at [[Columbia University]] working in [[number theory]] and [[automorphic forms]], particularly [[Iwasawa theory]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.math.columbia.edu/~urban/ | title=Eric Urban's Faculty Page | author=Eric Urban | website=Columbia University Department of Mathematics | access-date=2024-10-06 }}</ref>

==Career==
Urban received his PhD in mathematics from [[Paris-Sud University]] in 1994 under the supervision of [[Jacques Tilouine]].<ref name="mathgenealogy">{{MathGenealogy|id=30634}}</ref> He is a professor of mathematics at Columbia University.<ref name="directory">{{cite web|url=https://www.math.columbia.edu/people/directory/name/eric-urban/ |publisher=[[Columbia University]] |title=Eric Jean-Paul Urban » Department Directory |access-date=3 March 2020}}</ref>

==Research==
Together with [[Christopher Skinner]], Urban proved many cases of [[Main conjecture of Iwasawa theory|Iwasawa–Greenberg main conjecture]]s for a large class of [[modular form]]s.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Skinner |first1=Christopher |last2=Urban |first2=Eric |year=2014 |title=The Iwasawa Main Conjectures for GL2 |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00222-013-0448-1 |journal=Inventiones Mathematicae |language=en |volume=195 |issue=1 |pages=1–277 |doi=10.1007/s00222-013-0448-1 |bibcode=2014InMat.195....1S |s2cid=120848645 |issn=0020-9910|url-access=subscription }}</ref> As a consequence, for a [[modular elliptic curve]] over the [[rational number]]s, they prove that the vanishing of the [[Hasse–Weil L-function|Hasse–Weil ''L''-function]] ''L''(''E'',&nbsp;''s'') of ''E'' at ''s''&nbsp;=&nbsp;1 implies that the p-adic [[Selmer group]] of ''E'' is infinite. Combined with theorems of [[Benedict Gross|Gross]]-[[Don Zagier|Zagier]] and [[Victor Kolyvagin|Kolyvagin]], this gave a conditional proof (on the [[Tate–Shafarevich conjecture]]) of the conjecture that ''E'' has infinitely many rational points if and only if ''L''(''E'',&nbsp;1) =  0, a (weak) form of the [[Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]]. These results were used (in joint work with [[Manjul Bhargava]] and [[Wei Zhang (mathematician)|Wei Zhang]]) to prove that a positive proportion of elliptic curves satisfy the [[Birch–Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|last1=Bhargava|first1=Manjul|last2=Skinner|first2=Christopher|last3=Zhang|first3=Wei|date=2014-07-07|title=A majority of elliptic curves over $\mathbb Q$ satisfy the Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture|eprint=1407.1826|class=math.NT}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://mattbaker.blog/2014/03/10/the-bsd-conjecture-is-true-for-most-elliptic-curves/|title=The BSD conjecture is true for most elliptic curves|last=Baker|first=Matt|date=2014-03-10|website=Matt Baker's Math Blog|language=en|access-date=2019-02-24}}</ref>

==Awards==
Urban was awarded a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 2007.<ref name="Guggenheim">{{cite web |url= https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/eric-urban/ |title=Eric Urban |website=[[John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation]] |access-date=9 March 2021}}</ref>
